image.alt: The Disappearance of Gustavo Norman banner

paragraphs: 五名遊歷各處的冒險者被顯赫的貴族諾曼爵士弗雷德里克・諾曼透過眼線招募來到了他的住處。諾曼爵士說明，根據他的眼線，自己成年的兒子古斯塔夫據傳一個月前在洛森王國與麥丁頓王國邊界的艾爾諾村失蹤了，他和他的年輕妻子，同時也是古斯塔夫的青梅竹馬潘蜜拉十分擔心，因此重金禮聘冒險者們到艾爾諾村幫忙調查古斯塔夫的下落，並承諾只要能回報給他古斯塔夫的狀況，就能領取一人 10 枚白金幣的豐厚獎賞。
五名冒險者：喬拉拉、我的甜心烘衣機（以下簡稱甜心烘衣機）、小小小家亨、麥恩・奎瑞與安納戴克坐了一個月的馬車，終於抵達艾爾諾村，而車夫在放下他們後便離開了。

放眼望去，在艾爾諾村的住民幾乎都是妖精，但是仔細一看，其實他們都是半妖精。這裡與其說是村莊，更像是部落，村民都是居住在帳篷內。感到好奇的冒險者們拉了一名路人想要談話，卻發現對方不懂普通語。唯一懂妖精語的小小小家亨便成了大家的翻譯員。路人找來了一名名為多蘇，懂普通語的男子，帶領冒險者。和多蘇簡單交涉後，冒險者們大致知道了這裡主要的重要人物有長老（也可視為村長），同時是多蘇哥哥的巴蘇，以及宗教領袖教主大人。大夥兒也從多蘇那邊聽說了他最後一次見到古斯塔夫時是看見他和長老巴蘇吵架。大家先跟隨著多蘇來到了教主大人的營帳。
進入了營帳內，教主向大家自我介紹，自稱魯尼，並表示部落內的人都是月神教的忠誠信徒，部落內滿月時會舉行儀式，歡迎冒險者們一同參加。冒險者們也向教主詢問了關於古斯塔夫的狀況，他表示一兩個月前有見到過這名年輕的人類，而且他對當地的儀式也十分感興趣，但好像突然就失蹤了。
接著教主派了人帶領大家去找長老。營帳內，長老似乎正在忙著，對冒險者們的提問都不太正面回應。他表示自己見過古斯塔夫，但是古斯塔夫好像不見了，他也不清楚為什麼。
在眾人離開營帳後，躲藏在營帳內的喬拉拉發現長老喚來了幾個人。雖然聽不懂妖精語，但喬拉拉用自製的工具將聲音錄了下來，並向外傳遞給了在營帳門口的小小小家亨，內容大致是長老驚訝的告訴身邊的人竟然有人在調查古斯塔夫的事，要大家小心一點。

在喬拉拉變身成狗，被人抱離營帳後，大家在部落的樹林邊討論著接下來的計畫。大家先詢問到了可以住宿的地方：一個較鮮艷的大型營帳，營帳的主人叫馬法。馬法在將自己的其他客人趕走後，簡單和冒險者們聊了聊。他表示外地人來這裡都是他安排住宿，並向冒險者們透露他也曾接待過古斯塔夫。他表示古斯塔夫是個好孩子，卻因為對部落內的傳統以及儀式有所不滿，在爭吵中誤殺了前任長老而被暴民殺死。馬法帶著冒險者們來到了森林的深處前任長老納爾的墳前致意，而旁邊便是古斯塔夫的墳墓，不過他的墓碑上被人用妖精語塗鴉破壞。
馬法接著代冒險者們回到案發現場：滿月儀式的場地。廣場的正中央有個石製的圓形平台，散發出濃濃的血味與燒焦味。馬法說明平常儀式都在這裡進行，古斯塔夫死時雖然不是儀式當下，但是也是在這裡和村民起衝突的。此時，教主派的人找到了冒險者們，告知他們明天晚上會有一場滿月儀式，邀請他們參加。馬法表示不用擔心，一是絕對不會危及他們的生命。
回到馬法的大帳篷，眾人向他詢問村內滿月的儀式到底是什麼？馬法表示儀式的內容不太人道，他可以理解為何古斯塔夫會如此激烈的反對。而冒險者們在反覆推敲後認為儀式內容很有可能是獻祭當地的孩童。馬法找了三名小朋友，給了他們一人一枚金幣，請他們幫冒險者們搭帳篷。冒險者們也想起，在來到部落後，確實幾乎都沒有看到孩童。
帳篷搭好後，冒險者們和孩童們搭話，大略知道了這幾位看起來貧困的孩子住在哪裡，也簡單拜訪了一下，發現他們都家庭狀況似乎都不是太好。為了以防萬一，喬拉拉在這幾名孩童的營帳前設置了警報，擔心他們被當作獻祭的對象。
接著，冒險者們也詢問到了一家賣各式雜貨、材料的小店。店的裝飾低調，裡面的老闆是一名人類—是定居在這裡的唯一一名人類。他自我介紹名為寇久，告誡了冒險者們在部落內要特別小心，表示因為妖精生產力低，會誘拐來到這裡的外地人，讓他們為部落產下子代。因此今晚在這裡過夜，要特別注意。寇久也為喬拉拉準備了他所需要的各式工具與材料。
日落後，遠比大家認知更多的半妖精紛紛從帳篷內走了出來，在部落內唱著歌活動著。冒險者們思索著該直接離開部落，還是待到隔天參與儀式。最後，冒險者們決定早點開始休息，利用半夜的時間在部落內進行調查。
大家輪流守夜，喬拉拉也在營帳門口設置了警報器，卻意外被第一輪守夜的安納戴克玩壞了。在大家都睡著後喬拉拉和甜心烘衣機被偷偷闖入的民眾劫走，清醒後的小小小家亨、麥恩・奎瑞和安納戴克跑到了帳篷外。安納戴克到了樹林邊和附近的動物朋友溝通，請貓頭鷹們幫他找到兩位失蹤夥伴的蹤跡，並在樹下等待他們的回應。他也決定讓麥恩・奎瑞和小小小家亨先回帳篷等待。
麥恩・奎瑞和小小小家亨在往營帳的路途中撞見了兩名守衛，在小小小家亨溝通未果的情況下守衛和他們打了起來，居民們紛紛湧了上來，將兩人綑綁後抬走。
在得到了貓頭鷹的指點後，安納戴克準備前往喬拉拉和甜心烘衣機被綁走的地方，大約是儀式場地附近。他也從貓頭鷹給予的消息得知另外兩位夥伴似乎也遇害了。在儀式場地旁的樹丛，安納戴克小心觀察，沒發現一旁有人搭了他的肩膀，是寇久。

寇久透過心電感應傳話給安納戴克，表示自己願意來幫忙救他們。兩人觀察了前面的兩座帳篷，判斷右邊沒有人圍著的帳篷應該是甜心烘衣機和喬拉拉被安置的帳篷，而有一群人圍繞，正運送著東西進去的左側帳篷，很有可能就是小小小家亨和麥恩・奎瑞被運送的地方。繞到了右側帳篷旁邊，安納戴克割開了帳篷一側，兩人悄聲潛入，看見赤身裸體昏倒在地上的甜心烘衣機和喬拉拉，以及兩名正在談天的半妖精，一男一女。成功襲擊了男子，旁邊的女半妖精卻開始尖叫，帳篷外有其他半妖精開始進入，安納戴克和寇久只好趕緊把昏迷的兩人先行搬走並逃了出去，跑到了樹林邊緣。

另一方面，麥恩・奎瑞和小小小家亨被放到了地上，但手腳和嘴都被綁住了。麥恩・奎瑞聽見了半妖精們開始頌歌，他強忍住了不自覺想跟著吟唱的心，看見一名穿著華麗的半妖精領著一名看起來富裕健全的孩童從帳篷深處走了出來，向大家致意。眾人唱著歌，隨著他們走出了帳篷外。小小小家亨成功解開了束縛，卻像是被歌聲控制住了一般，也唱起了歌，跟著大家走了出去。麥恩・奎瑞好不容易解開了束縛，趕緊在帳篷內尋找武器，卻只有找到幾塊碎玻璃和石頭，便趕緊朝反方向開始逃亡。
樹林邊，甜心烘衣機恢復了意識，喬拉拉卻還在昏迷。甜心烘衣機試圖扛起喬拉拉卻因為身體太過勞累而失敗。安納戴克提議讓甜心烘衣機先逃出部落，而寇久將喬拉拉先藏起來。安納戴克則先在附近隨時注意現況。然而，在大家分頭離開後，安納戴克卻抵抗不住半妖精歌曲的力量，也朝著儀式現場靠近。滿月儀式似乎提前一天開始了。
甜心烘衣機成功逃到了樹林邊界，卻聽到了大聲的警報，以及遠處傳來有人吶喊的聲音。他趕緊用自己的魔法生出了火，將四處的樹林點燃，然後繼續逃亡。
麥恩・奎瑞也靠著自己對野外的認知，逃進了另一側的樹林，並找到了洞穴休息。
安納戴克看見小小小家亨也在儀式現場，卻控制不住自己的身體，無法前去救他。在儀式最後他看見大部分的半妖精都昏倒了下來，小小小家亨還撐著身體搖晃著。模糊的意識下，他感受到了有人在搖晃著他的肩。寇久用力的搖晃著安納戴克，而安納戴克終於清醒，撐著身體去拯救小小小家亨。成功將小小小家亨搖醒後，安納戴克發現寇久已經倒下，身上的傷口似乎已經沒救了。他將寇久的眼睛闔上後，便帶著小小小家亨逃入了森林。
迷迷糊糊，喬拉拉醒來了。他發現自己在寇久的店舖裡，附近一個人都沒有。帳篷外，只聽見了小孩的哭聲。他隨著哭聲找到了一名半妖精小女孩，而小女孩也指引了他找到另外兩名半妖精小孩子。喬拉拉背著一個小孩，兩手再各牽一個，從森林逃了出去。
冒險者們紛紛逃離了艾爾諾村以及這場夢魘，幾個月後終於回到了爵士家休養，也領到了他們應得的賞金。而喬拉拉也發現了自己似乎懷有了身孕。後來，爵士也告訴冒險者，艾爾諾村，似乎消失了。

Five traveling adventurers were recruited through the agents of the prominent noble Syr Frederick Norman and brought to his residence. Syr Norman explained that, according to his informants, his adult son Gustavo had disappeared a month earlier in El’Nore, a village on the border between the kingdoms of Lawson and Mattington. He and his young wife Pamela, who had also been Gustavo’s childhood friend, were deeply worried. He therefore hired the adventurers at great expense to investigate Gustavo’s whereabouts, promising each of them ten platinum pieces if they returned with news of his condition.

The five adventurers—Jorara, My Sweet Drying Machine (MSDM), Little Little Little Jiaheng, Mine Quarry, and Anedak—finally reached El’Nore after a month-long carriage ride. Their driver departed as soon as he had dropped them off.

At first glance, nearly everyone in El’Nore appeared to be an elf, though closer inspection showed they were all half-elves. It felt less like a village than a tribe, with every resident living in a tent. The curious adventurers tried speaking to a passerby, only to discover that he did not understand Common. Little Little Little Jiaheng, the only member who spoke Elvish, became their interpreter. The passerby fetched a Common-speaking man named Dosuu to guide them. From their brief conversation, the adventurers learned that the tribe’s principal figures were its elder, or village chief, Basuu—Dosuu’s older brother—and a religious leader known as the Hierarch. Dosuu also said that the last time he saw Gustavo, Gustavo was arguing with Elder Basuu. The group first followed Dosuu to the Hierarch’s tent.

Inside, the Hierarch introduced himself as Luny. He said the tribe were devoted followers of the Moon God and performed a ritual at every full moon, inviting the adventurers to join them. When asked about Gustavo, Luny said he had seen the young human a month or two earlier. Gustavo had been very interested in the local ritual, but then seemed to vanish without warning.

The Hierarch then sent someone to take them to the elder. Basuu seemed busy and avoided giving direct answers. He said he had met Gustavo, but Gustavo had apparently disappeared and he did not know why.

After the others left, Jorara remained hidden in the tent and saw the elder summon several people. Though unable to understand Elvish, Jorara recorded their voices with a homemade device and relayed the sound to Little Little Little Jiaheng outside. The gist was that Basuu was alarmed that someone had come to investigate Gustavo and warned everyone to be careful.

After Jorara transformed into a dog and was carried out of the tent, the group discussed their next move at the forest’s edge. They first found lodging in a large, brightly colored tent owned by Mafa. After evicting his other guests, Mafa spoke briefly with the adventurers. He said he arranged lodging for all outsiders and revealed that Gustavo had once stayed with him. Gustavo had been a good young man, but his objections to the tribe’s traditions and ritual led to an argument in which he accidentally killed the former elder. A mob then killed Gustavo. Mafa led the group deep into the forest to pay respects at former elder Nal’s grave. Gustavo’s grave stood beside it, though its headstone had been defaced with Elvish graffiti.

Mafa next took the adventurers to the scene of the incident: the full-moon ritual grounds. At the center of the plaza stood a circular stone platform reeking of blood and burned flesh. Mafa explained that rituals were normally held there. Gustavo had not died during a ritual, but it was there that he clashed with the villagers. A messenger from the Hierarch then found the adventurers and invited them to a full-moon ritual the following evening. Mafa assured them there was no need to worry and that the ritual would never endanger their lives.

Back in Mafa’s large tent, the group asked what the village’s full-moon ritual actually involved. Mafa admitted that it was inhumane and that he understood Gustavo’s fierce opposition. After considering the clues, the adventurers suspected that local children were sacrificed. Mafa hired three children, paying each a gold piece to pitch tents for the adventurers. The group then realized they had indeed seen almost no children since arriving.

Once the tents were ready, the adventurers spoke with the children, learned roughly where the visibly impoverished youngsters lived, and paid brief visits. None appeared to come from a stable home. As a precaution, Jorara placed alarms outside their tents, fearing they might be selected as sacrifices.

The adventurers also heard about a small shop selling sundries and materials. Its decoration was subdued, and its owner was a human—the only human settled in the tribe. Introducing himself as Kojo, he warned them to be especially careful. Elves had low birth rates, he said, so the tribe abducted outsiders and forced them to produce children. They should be particularly vigilant if they stayed overnight. Kojo also prepared the tools and materials Jorara needed.

After sunset, far more half-elves than expected emerged from their tents, singing and moving throughout the settlement. The adventurers debated leaving immediately or staying for the next day’s ritual. In the end, they decided to rest early and investigate the tribe around midnight.

The group took turns keeping watch. Jorara placed an alarm at the entrance, but Anedak accidentally broke it during the first watch. Once everyone was asleep, intruders abducted Jorara and MSDM. Little Little Little Jiaheng, Mine Quarry, and Anedak woke and ran outside. At the forest’s edge, Anedak spoke with nearby animals and asked the owls to find his two missing companions, then waited beneath a tree for their answer. He sent Mine Quarry and Little Little Little Jiaheng back to the tent.

On their way, Mine Quarry and Little Little Little Jiaheng encountered two guards. When Jiaheng failed to reason with them, a fight broke out. Villagers poured in, bound the pair, and carried them away.

Guided by the owls, Anedak headed toward the place where Jorara and MSDM were being held, somewhere near the ritual grounds. The owls also suggested that his other two companions had been captured. As Anedak watched carefully from the bushes beside the grounds, someone unexpectedly placed a hand on his shoulder. It was Kojo.

Kojo spoke telepathically to Anedak and offered to help with the rescue. Studying two tents ahead, they concluded that the unguarded tent on the right held MSDM and Jorara, while the crowded tent on the left, into which people were carrying something, likely held Little Little Little Jiaheng and Mine Quarry. Anedak cut through the side of the right-hand tent, and the two slipped inside. They found MSDM and Jorara unconscious and naked on the ground while a male and female half-elf chatted nearby. They successfully struck the man, but the woman began screaming and other half-elves rushed in. Anedak and Kojo hurriedly carried the two unconscious adventurers out and fled to the forest’s edge.

Meanwhile, Mine Quarry and Little Little Little Jiaheng lay on the ground with their hands, feet, and mouths bound. Mine Quarry heard the half-elves begin a chant and fought the urge to sing along. A richly dressed half-elf emerged from deep within the tent, leading a healthy, well-to-do child, and greeted the crowd. Still singing, everyone followed them outside. Little Little Little Jiaheng escaped his bonds, but seemed enthralled by the song; he began singing too and walked out with the others. Mine Quarry finally freed himself and searched the tent for a weapon, finding only shards of glass and stones before fleeing in the opposite direction.

At the forest’s edge, MSDM regained consciousness, but Jorara did not. Exhaustion kept MSDM from lifting Jorara. Anedak suggested that MSDM escape the tribe first while Kojo hid Jorara, and that he himself remain nearby to watch events unfold. Once they separated, however, Anedak could not resist the half-elves’ song and began moving toward the ritual grounds. The full-moon ritual seemed to have begun a day early.
MSDM reached the edge of the forest, only to hear a blaring alarm and distant shouts. He hurriedly conjured fire, set the surrounding woods ablaze, and continued his escape.
Drawing on his wilderness knowledge, Mine Quarry fled into the forest on the other side and found a cave in which to rest.

Anedak saw Little Little Little Jiaheng at the ritual but could not control his body well enough to save him. Near the ritual’s end, most of the half-elves collapsed while Jiaheng remained unsteadily on his feet. Through the haze, Anedak felt someone shaking his shoulder. Kojo shook him hard until he finally came to his senses and forced himself toward Jiaheng. After waking him, Anedak saw that Kojo had fallen and that his wounds were beyond saving. He closed Kojo’s eyes, then led Jiaheng into the forest.

Jorara awoke in a daze inside Kojo’s shop, with no one nearby. Outside the tent, he heard only a child crying. He followed the sound to a young half-elf girl, who led him to two more half-elf children. Carrying one child on his back and holding another by each hand, Jorara escaped through the forest.

The adventurers escaped El’Nore and its nightmare. Months later, they returned to Syr Norman’s residence to recover and received their promised reward. Jorara also discovered that he appeared to be pregnant. Later, the noble told the adventurers that El’Nore itself seemed to have vanished.
